To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the random graph theory based key pre-distribution scheme is a good solution to the problem of key management in wireless sensor networks.

(i) the key distribution problem for sensor networks can be solved using random key pre-distributions, and (ii) a key pre-distribution scheme based on random graphs can be used to provide secure communications in sensor networks.
the key pre-distribution scheme based on random geometric graph is not effective in the sparse network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
revisiting random graph-based key management schemes for sensor networks.
revisiting random key pre distribution schemes for wireless sensor network.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed schemes are not secure in the face of an active adversary and the security of the proposed schemes is not guaranteed in the face of a passive adversary.
the random graph theory is a very powerful tool for the study of key pre-distribution in wireless sensor networks.
random key pre-distributions schemes are not suitable for large scale sensor network applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the key distribution problem in wireless sensor networks is a very challenging problem.
the proposed scheme is a good alternative for the random key pre-distributions schemes for wireless sensor network.

we have proposed a novel random graph theory-based key pre-distribution scheme for wireless sensor networks, which is more efficient than the previous schemes in terms of storage, communication and computation costs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree of the underlying physical network has significant impact on the security of the network.

, in a sensor network where the nodes are randomly distributed and the network is sparse, the performance of key management schemes based on random graph models is very poor and the security is not as high as expected.
, in the case of sparse networks, the random graph theory is not sufficient to provide a secure network.
